messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — auth graph telemetry is showing a mismatch between console attribution and API logs for delegated service-account tokens. :eyes:
azra: ugh, saw a couple alerts too. which env/service?
maria: saw this on staging when we ran the multi-tenant load test (proj-42 -> org-9). console shows project attribution but billing/usage pipeline attributes to org fallback.
sanjay: exact. console and the billing pipeline disagree on 'effective_project' for SA-exchange flows. example event we got from the API pipeline:
```
issuer: org:9
project: proj:42
principal: sa:123
exchange_path: /v1/token/exchange
route: /v1/embeddings
quota_key: org-9
```
azra: the quota_key coming out as org-9 is the problem — we expect quota_key to be project-42 when a project-scoped SA is used. Might be a routing policy edge where the proxy drops the project claim during impersonation.
lee: could be a timing window on claim propagation. Are we sure the introspection service is returning project_claim consistently? any sampling traces?
sanjay: I pulled a couple traces. proxy -> auth-resolver -> quota-service. In some traces the exchange flow hits the cache miss path and returns only org claim. When cache miss + async metadata enrichment happens, the console later shows project, but billing got the earlier event.
azra: so it's a race between enrichment and emitting metrics. Two options: 1) buffer emission until enrichment completes for exchange flows, or 2) include a best-effort 'later_update' telemetry event that billing can reconcile.
maria: buffering hurts latency SLOs for small requests. We should avoid holding request paths. I prefer emitting quickly and sending a reconciliation 'update' event if enrichment arrives later.
lee: reconciliation sounds safer operationally. billing can apply idempotent updates. Need fields: original_event_id, effective_project (optional), enriched_at, prev_quota_key.
sanjay: agree. also adding a 'claim_origin' tag so downstream can decide whether to trust an org-level fallback or a project-level claim.
azra: implementation notes: auth-resolver can emit two events — initial auth_event and auth_enrichment_event. auth_enrichment_event should include resolved_project and a boolean 'final=true'.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: auth-resolver v2.14 -> staging at 2026-03-22T18:30Z (will post status updates).
maria: we also need console UX changes — show a note on request logs when an enrichment update arrives ("project attribution updated from org-9 to proj-42 at 18:29:03").
lee: +1. Also add a small telemetry dashboard tile: "reconciled auth attributions / hour" so SRE and billing can monitor.
sanjay: I'll draft the telemetry schema (event names, fields) and a small migration plan for consumers. Plan: (A) auth-resolver emits enrichment events, (B) billing pipeline accepts reconciliation events idempotently, (C) console shows update history, (D) quick canary in staging then prod sweep.
azra: ping me once draft is ready, I can add tests to simulate cache miss + enrichment race.
maria: thanks. @sanjay can you add the reconciliation schema to the thread so we can review? :thumbsup:
